relevant_files.summary: Release gate now conditionally skips strict Windows packaging dry-run when compatibility prerequisites are absent. This changes release hard-gate semantics without direct code-level tests.
Main integration workflow gained the same packaging prerequisite branch, so CI enforcement behavior can differ between hydrated and fresh checkouts.
Delivery contract was widened to require the new local desktop launcher entrypoints and docs anchors.
Authority alignment rules now enforce the launcher contract across README, desktop README, and runbook surfaces.
Governance-script regression coverage was expanded heavily and now covers launcher scripts, package.json exposure, and docs anchors.
Adds `local:*` launcher entrypoints and participates in both release gate and local launcher contract.
New PowerShell launcher manages gateway reuse, port fallback, desktop process reuse, and binary/tauri-dev fallback. It affects local developer startup flow, not the shipped desktop runtime path.
Only changes the embedded application version constant from 9.0.4 to 9.0.6. Runtime behavior is unchanged apart from reported version metadata.
Desktop bundle version metadata sync only.
Cargo lockfile synchronized to the new version; build metadata only.
Release sign-off docs now describe Windows packaging lanes that may be conditional after the workflow change.
New test-tier documentation broadens docs footprint but does not change executable behavior.

module_map.assessment: Narrow change. Only app/version metadata was updated to 9.0.6; no routing, state, workflow, desktop UI, or backend behavior changed here.
Mixed narrow change: version sync is low risk, but package.json also exposes new local launcher commands.
New operational surface for Windows local bring-up. Useful but not the main shipped runtime path. Risk is localized to developer workflow, port/process handling, and local validation behavior.
Release contract changed materially, but it is strongly covered by focused Python tests. This area is safety-critical because it defines what the project considers a valid release surface.

Most important risk hotspot in the current delta. The strict Windows packaging lane can now be skipped depending on prerequisite hydration. In this checkout `desktop/src-tauri/bin/niko-gateway-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe` exists, but `git ls-files` shows that prerequisite is not tracked, so clean CI checkouts may take a different branch than the current local workspace.

key_findings.finding: The current source worktree is effectively clean; the only git delta is the untracked current team-session directory.
key_findings.impact: There is no active uncommitted product-source conflict risk. The decision is about committed delta since the last green evidence, not dirty local edits.

key_findings.finding: Seven commits landed after the 2026-04-13 17:01:51 +08:00 green release evidence baseline.
key_findings.impact: The old evidence is no longer an exact HEAD proof. A decision to skip full regression must rely on risk classification, not on exact snapshot identity.

key_findings.finding: Most of the file-count breadth is documentation and contract-synchronization churn, not core runtime logic churn.
key_findings.impact: The delta looks broad on paper but is not a broad product rewrite. That weakens the case for a blanket full regression driven purely by product-runtime change volume.

key_findings.finding: The highest-risk technical change is the new conditional CI logic that can skip strict Windows packaging dry-run when compatibility prerequisites are absent.
key_findings.impact: Release confidence can diverge between hydrated local environments and fresh CI checkouts. This is a release/infra risk hotspot even though it does not change user-facing runtime behavior.

key_findings.finding: The new local desktop launcher workflow is developer-facing and tightly scoped, and the associated governance contract is backed by extensive Python tests.
key_findings.impact: The launcher addition increases local workflow surface area, but it is not evidence of a core runtime regression requiring whole-product retest by itself.

key_findings.finding: The runtime-facing code change inside `src-ts` is only a version constant bump to 9.0.6.
key_findings.impact: There is no sign here of new backend behavior, workflow engine logic, route changes, or desktop UI state changes after the green evidence.

risk_classification.broad_vs_narrow: Narrow in executable runtime behavior; broad in release-adjacent, documentation, and governance surfaces.
risk_classification.already_covered_vs_uncertain: Governance-script changes appear well-covered by targeted tests; CI workflow branch changes are the least directly covered part of the delta.

recent_workflow_context.relevance: Recorded a successful run of authority alignment, delivery gate, src-ts local checks, desktop local checks, and desktop packaging dry-run on the prior release handoff baseline.
Older analysis had dirty-worktree caveats but bounded the earlier refactor scope; that dirty-worktree condition is no longer present today.

questions_for_analysis: Does the team require fresh exact-head release evidence whenever CI/release-gate semantics change, even if core runtime code does not?
Is the new packaging-prerequisite skip path acceptable without an explicit targeted validation on a clean checkout that lacks the compatibility artifact?
Should the decision distinguish ordinary development confidence from formal release sign-off confidence, since the current delta is mostly release/governance-oriented?
